evidence.text: Asset freeze (also called blocking). Nobody may pay, hold or move the target's money or property. Export controls. Sensitive goods need a licence, which is usually refused for listed buyers. Sector bans. Whole kinds of trade are cut, such as buying Russian oil above a price cap. Ownership rules. Companies owned by a listed party can be blocked without being named (section 2). Secondary sanctions (pressure on outsiders). Since Executive Order 14114 (December 2023), the US can sanction a foreign bank that handles significant deals for Russia's military industry. Foreign banks now have their own reason to check. A battlefield-goods list. The US, EU, UK and Japan share the Common High Priority List: 50 product types, by customs code, found in Russian missiles and drones. Semiconductor chips (integrated circuits) are in the top tier. Humanitarian exemptions. Since December 2022, food, medicine and aid are carved out of all UN asset freezes, and the US issues matching general licences.

evidence.text: 3 · The tricks Almost every trick does the same thing: it breaks the match between a listed name and a transaction. Below are six, each with an example from our own work or an official source. 1. Route through a third country Goods that can no longer go straight to Russia are sold to a neighbour first, then passed on. Our data: countries' own reports to the UN show chip exports to Russia jumping from almost nothing. Kyrgyzstan: about $0 a year in 2019 to 2021, then $13.5M in 2023. Kazakhstan: $18.3M in 2022. Armenia: $13.1M in 2022. Diagram 3: third-country routing Chip makers sell to Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan and Armenia, which pass the chips on to Russia. Each middle country's own reported chip exports to Russia rose from about zero to more than 13 million dollars. The direct route is restricted after February 2022. Diagram 3. Chip exports to Russia as each middle country itself reported them to UN Comtrade. The paperwork shows where goods were declared, not the road they took. 2. Set up front companies, then replace them New firms with no history do the trading. When one gets noticed, another takes over. Official example: the US Treasury's own entry for RM Design and Development (Kyrgyzstan) says it was established on 17 March 2022, 21 days after the invasion. The US listed it in July 2023. 3. Stay just under 50%, or hide a company in the middle A stake under the line is not blocked automatically, and an unnamed subsidiary does not show up in a name search. 4. Relabel the goods Describe a controlled item as something harmless, or file it under a different product code. Official example: in April 2026 the US Treasury described a broker shipping fentanyl ingredients labelled as "safe chemicals". 5. Transfer at sea and fly a false flag Oil is pumped from ship to ship out at sea, and tankers register under flags they are not entitled to. Official and research examples: 113 tankers under false flags carried €4.7bn of Russian oil in the first nine months of 2025. One tanker in our data changed its name five times. 6.
